title: Closed-pushforward cohomology comparison preserves connecting maps
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [def-sc-zariski-site, def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Define $(i_*D)(U)=D(U\cap Z)$ for every open $U\subseteq X$. Since $i_*$ is exact [lem-sc-closed-immersion-pushforward-exact], there is an image short exact sequence $0\to i_*A\to i_*B\to i_*C\to0$. The functors $T^p(D)=H^p(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},i_*D)$, with connecting maps from image sequences, form a delta-functor, and in degree zero identify with $H^0(Z_{\mathrm{Zar}},D)$. Let $t^p:H^p(Z_{\mathrm{Zar}},D)\to H^p(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},i_*D)$ be the unique morphism of delta-functors whose degree-zero component is this identity; each $t^p$ is an isomorphism. For every global section $c\in H^0(Z_{\mathrm{Zar}},C)$, one has $t^1(\delta_Z(c))=\delta_X(i_*c)$. In particular, if $C=\mathbf Z_Z$ is the constant integer sheaf and $u:\mathbf Z_X\to i_*\mathbf Z_Z$ is restriction, the boundary of $1$ for the pullback of the image sequence along $u$ is $t^1(\delta_Z(1))\in H^1(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},i_*A)$.

proof.text: Applying exact $i_*$ to the short exact sequence gives the image short exact sequence by [lem-sc-closed-immersion-pushforward-exact].

source.place: Lemma 02UV proof: exactness of direct image

proof.text: The functors $T^p(D)=H^p(X,i_*D)$ with image-sequence connecting maps form a delta-functor by exactness of $i_*$ and the natural long exact cohomology sequence [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Their degree-zero functor is naturally $H^0(Z,D)$ because $(i_*D)(X)=D(Z)$. The source $H^p(Z,-)$ is universal by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]. The target is universal by [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal], since for an injective $I$ on $Z$, [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] gives $T^p(I)=H^p(Z,I)=0$ for $p>0$. Hence the unique morphism $t^p$ with identity degree-zero component exists and is an isomorphism, with inverse supplied by the two universal properties.

source.place: Lemma 02UV, comparison as a morphism of cohomological delta-functors

proof.text: By the defining equation for a morphism of delta-functors [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor], $t^1(\delta_Z(c))=\delta_X(i_*c)$. For $C=\mathbf Z_Z$ and $c=1$, $u(1)=i_*1$ because $u$ is restriction. The pulled-back sequence maps to the image sequence by $(\mathrm{id},?,u)$, so naturality of connecting maps [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] identifies its boundary of $1$ with $\delta_X(i_*1)=t^1(\delta_Z(1))$.
